trait_policy.denominator: Unique deck Characters; exclude Leaders, Actions, Items, copies, and temporarily gained Traits.
trait_policy.notes: Traits are exact labels, never automatic abilities. Zero is valid. Actions, Items, and Leaders may carry useful Traits, but this pool prints them only on Characters. Human remains unprinted audit metadata. Limits are design guidance, not deckbuilding restrictions.

traits.name: Animal
traits.meaning: An animal Character, including an explicitly animal Undead Character.

traits.name: Undead
traits.meaning: A Character whose fiction explicitly includes returning from death. Survival alone does not qualify.

traits.name: Construct
traits.meaning: An animated, built, or manufactured Character. Ordinary Items are not Constructs.

traits.name: Rat
traits.meaning: A rat, printed alongside Animal when both apply. Other scavenging animals are not Rats.

traits.name: Kid
traits.meaning: A child or teen in the depicted Character concept.

traits.name: Parent
traits.meaning: A parent or grandparent, without implying a separate Human rule.

traits.name: Criminal
traits.meaning: A Character depicted committing theft, fraud, or another crime. A job, wealth, or an annoying personality is insufficient.

traits.name: Musician
traits.meaning: A musical performer. Road crew and general entertainers are not automatically Musicians.

traits.name: Pirate
traits.meaning: A deliberately pirate-themed Character. A pun in a title does not grant this Trait.

traits.name: Scout
traits.meaning: A member of the fictional Scout troop, including its quartermaster.

traits.name: HOA
traits.meaning: A member of the fictional homeowners association or its administration. General authority figures do not qualify automatically.

traits.name: Daredevil
traits.meaning: A Character who deliberately performs dangerous stunts.

traits.name: Wrestler
traits.meaning: A participating backyard wrestler. Fans, referees, and support staff do not qualify merely by proximity.

traits.name: Scavenger
traits.meaning: A Character who obtains supplies or food from discarded material.

traits.name: Builder
traits.meaning: A Character who builds or repairs things, however questionable the workmanship.

traits.name: Hacker
traits.meaning: A Character whose depicted activity involves exploiting or manipulating computer systems.

traits.name: Clown
traits.meaning: An actual clown performer. Being foolish is insufficient.

traits.name: Magician
traits.meaning: A stage-magic or escape performer; no supernatural rules are implied.

keywords.name: Hothead
keywords.definition: This Character may Attack in the Round it enters play.
keywords.limits: Does not Ready it, grant an extra Attack, allow Rotate activations on arrival, or override a cannot-Attack effect. A gained Hothead works the same way while it lasts.

keywords.name: Defiant
keywords.status: Renamed from the old Explosive rule; printed playtest keyword
keywords.definition: This Character retaliates when it Blocks even if the incoming Attack Defeats it.
keywords.limits: Only a Blocker receives this exception. Use its Power immediately before it left play. Slowpoke prevents this retaliation.

keywords.name: Explosive
keywords.definition: When this Character is Defeated, deal 1 damage to each opposing Character.
keywords.limits: This is a Defeat trigger, not retaliation. It affects opposing Characters in play, not Leaders, Items, or your Characters. Resolve it with other pending Defeat triggers, after the Attack damage and retaliation checkpoints when Defeated during an Attack.

keywords.name: Slowpoke
keywords.definition: This Character does not retaliate when it Blocks.
keywords.limits: It can still Attack. If attacked directly while Rotated, it retaliates if it survives. If it also has Defiant, Slowpoke prevents its blocking retaliation.

keywords.name: Sucker Punch
keywords.definition: This Character may Attack Ready opposing Characters.
keywords.limits: Such an Attack is direct, cannot be Blocked, and follows normal rotation, damage and retaliation. The entry-Round Attack restriction still applies.

keywords.name: Sneaky
keywords.definition: Playing this card from your hand on your Turn does not use that Turn. Pay its normal Cost; only one Sneaky Play may occur per Turn.
keywords.limits: Finish the Play and all its triggers before taking the normal Turn action. It grants neither an extra Turn nor a Response window. A free Play from another zone cannot use Sneaky.

keywords.name: Cloak
keywords.definition: Rotate: Turn this Character face down until the end of the Round. While face down, it cannot Attack, Block, Activate, be chosen, take damage, or be Defeated.
keywords.limits: The face-down Character remains in play, keeps its damage, orientation and attachments, and counts as a Character. Its printed abilities are inactive. Reveal it at end of Round before Round-limited effects expire; check Defeat when revealed. It cannot Activate this keyword the Round it enters play.

keywords.name: Stack
keywords.definition: When Playing this Character, you may put it atop one of your Characters; pay its normal Cost. The two face-up layers form one Character.
keywords.limits: At most two layers. Top supplies Power, Guard, Traits, and attack/block restrictions. Both layers supply abilities; resolve simultaneous layer triggers bottom to top. Keep damage and orientation; the pile leaves play together, except explicit card text. Stacking does not Ready or grant an extra Attack.

notes: Zombie remains a possible later sub-Trait. The present six-card Undead package works without a second near-duplicate label.
Rat does not imply Animal, and gaining Undead does not grant Zombie or remove existing Traits. Print every label an effect should see.
Magician, Hacker, and Wrestler are deliberately concentrated in one Style for this pool. Their support cards work without a matching Trait and can be paired with another Style.
Three Character appearances are 2.8% of 108, an intentional soft-floor allowance. Do not pad the roster to satisfy rounded percentages.
No Trait is a Leader requirement. Leader Traits remain future card design, not a mandatory four-label quota.
Jerry-Rig remains earmarked. Encore, Pick a Card, Scrounge, and related names are card titles, not global keywords. Response remains outside this revision.
